name: You Make Me Feel Like A Natural Woman

podcast.body: This classic hit was one of Franklin's greatest ever. She famously performed it live at the 2015 Kennedy Center Honors, where she was celebrating Carole King (who co-wrote the song), captivating the audience and moving President Obama to tears, dropping her fur coat on stage as a gesture of honor from gospel music. "writer of one of Franklin's greatest ever hits, which the Queen of Seoul stepped out on stage, clad in a fur coat to perform live."

podcast.body: This standout hit was specially ordered by Atlantic producer Jerry Wexler from famed Brill Building songwriters Carole King and Gerry Goffin, based on a title Wexler conceived for Aretha. Featuring gospel-style piano by Spooner Oldham, backing vocals from The Sweet Inspirations and Aretha's sister Irma Franklin, and strings arranged by Ralph Burns, the song became an anthem of female self-actualization. It reached number eight on the Hot 100 and number two on the R&B chart in November 1967. "You Make Me Feel You Make Me Feel Like A Natural Woman, a natural woman reached number eight on the hot 100 and number two on the R&B chart in November 67."
